topics.title: Image Enhancement
topics.description: We develop computational and learning-based methods to recover informative images from noisy, incomplete, or artifact-corrupted measurements. By combining imaging physics with neural representations and generative priors, we study restoration and reconstruction across projection and image domains. Our goal is to improve image quality while preserving anatomical structure, natural texture, and information relevant to downstream tasks.

topics.title: Trustworthy AI
topics.description: We study how AI models can recognize the limits of their predictions and remain reliable when data, acquisition conditions, or application settings change. Our research uses uncertainty estimation to assess model confidence and guide the use of learned information alongside physical knowledge and measured evidence. We aim to develop adaptable AI methods that preserve meaningful structures, reduce unsupported predictions, and support reliable use beyond the training distribution.

topics.title: Dental Panoramic
topics.description: We develop AI for dental panoramic radiographs, with diagnosis support and report generation as complementary research directions. Our work on lesion detection, anatomically guided lesion synthesis, and report-guided annotation addresses limited labeled data and the need to connect visual findings with clinical language. Building on these methods, we aim to support image-grounded reporting that communicates relevant dental findings consistently and clearly.
tasks: Dental lesion detection and diagnosis support
Anatomically guided lesion synthesis and data augmentation

topics.title: Physics-based System Development
topics.description: We develop CT imaging systems by jointly designing acquisition geometry, calibration, and image reconstruction. Our work includes carbon-nanotube-based multisource architectures and compact C-arm CT prototypes, with an emphasis on expanding anatomical coverage and making effective use of measured projections. From source–detector alignment and detector correction to volume fusion, we integrate imaging physics and computational methods and evaluate complete imaging pipelines through simulation and prototype experiments.

Field-of-view extension and multisource volume fusion

topics.title: Image Quality Evaluation
topics.description: We quantify image quality through physical measurements, task performance, and human perception. Our methods characterize spatial resolution and noise using the modulation transfer function (MTF) and noise power spectrum (NPS), while model observers assess how well images support signal detection and discrimination. We also investigate learning-based, no-reference quality assessment aligned with radiologist judgments, providing complementary tools to evaluate imaging systems, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction or enhancement algorithms.
tasks: Local NPS estimation and noise characterization
Model observers and task-based image quality assessment
Human perception and no-reference quality assessment
